name: Freeport-McMoRan (fcx.com): Autonomous Haulage and AI Recognition at Bagdad
title: Freeport-McMoRan (fcx.com): Autonomous Haulage and AI Recognition at Bagdad
answer: Freeport-McMoRan's website documents its Bagdad, Arizona mine becoming the first major US mine with fully autonomous haulage, with 33 driverless trucks and more than 50 million tons moved, alongside its 31st place ranking in the Fortune AIQ 50 for measurable AI impact. It is a company news source rather than a technical study, but it gives a detailed operational account of autonomy at scale.

sections.body: This is the corporate website of Freeport-McMoRan, the US copper major, read across 60 pages in October 2026. The relevant material is a series of dated news features published between January 2025 and May 2026, plus a promotional page on the company's role as America's Copper Champion. The features track the Bagdad Autonomous Haulage System in Arizona from equipment conversion through full implementation, and one article covers the company's placement in the Fortune AIQ 50 ranking. The pages are company communications rather than independent reporting or technical papers.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The January 2025 feature describes preparations at Bagdad, where Haul Truck 230, a Caterpillar 793-D, became the first in the fleet converted for autonomous operation, with 33 driverless trucks planned to handle more than 95 percent of haulage by the end of the year. A new command center and two light vehicle tunnels were under construction, and training used a simulator built from video, photographs and drone footage of the actual mine. Testing began in an isolation zone in February, focused on safety such as automatic stopping for obstructions and staying within routes at proper speeds. By May 2025 the command center was online, operating 24/7 and combining dispatch with autonomous control, with 15 trucks having moved more than 3 million tons since March. The October 2025 feature reports full implementation of the 33-truck fleet from August, with seven staffed trucks continuing in a separate area, and a commitment that no displaced drivers would lose their jobs. By May 2026 the fleet had passed 50 million tons moved and was described as the largest autonomous fleet in North America. A separate October 2025 article reports Freeport ranked 31st of 50 in the first Fortune AIQ 50 ranking and second in the energy sector.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that 33 driverless haul trucks were planned to cover more than 95 percent of Bagdad's haulage, that the fleet reached 15 trucks and more than 3 million tons moved by May 2025, and that it surpassed 50 million tons by spring 2026. It reports that 217 haul truck drivers had found new roles as of mid-September 2025, with about 80 moving to shovels and other equipment and 15 retrained for the autonomous system, against a stated goal of zero job loss for more than 200 drivers. Freeport ranked 31st of 50 in the Fortune AIQ 50 and second in the energy sector. The company page states Freeport supplies approximately 70 percent of refined copper produced domestically and that its mines accounted for approximately 60 percent of domestic copper production in 2025.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in mining, this source is a rare operator-level account of autonomy moving from trial to full production. It gives concrete milestones, tonnages and timelines for a large copper mine, describes the supporting infrastructure of command center, communications networks, widened roads and isolation zones, and shows how safety testing was staged before scaling. The workforce transition detail, including retraining into autonomous system roles, is the kind of material usually absent from vendor claims. The Fortune AIQ 50 placement also signals how the company's broader AI adoption is being assessed externally.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: This is company-published material, so it presents the programme in a favourable light and offers no independent verification of performance or safety outcomes. It is largely about autonomous haulage rather than machine learning in processing, and it gives no technical detail on models, algorithms or data infrastructure. The Fortune AIQ 50 article reports the ranking and its methodology but not the underlying scores. The copper demand and economic impact figures come from a promotional page, and the impact studies are attributed to an external institute without further detail.
